title: Negation and scope
subtitle: Ask exactly which word, phrase, or clause is negated.
overview: οὐ commonly negates indicative assertions, while μή is common with non-indicative forms and several dependent constructions. Scope matters as much as the particle itself.
Mark whether the negation applies to one verb, a participle, an infinitive, or a contrasted clause before translating.

items.grc: οὐκ ἔστιν φόβος ἐν τῇ ἀγάπῃ.
items.en: There is no fear in love.
Do not judge, so that you may not be judged.
